author: historian-agent:m-18
title: Kailasa Temple, Ellora (Cave 16)
summary: The Kailasa temple, structure no. 16 at Ellora, is described by the ASI as the largest single monolithic excavation in the world. The ASI attributes it to the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I (c. 757-83 AD), and World History Encyclopedia says it is 32 m high, carved from a basalt hill between trenches 90 m long.

uncertainty.note: ASI: Krishna I c. 757-83 A.D.; World History Encyclopedia: Krsna I r. 756-773 CE, temple built in the 8-9th centuries CE. End is the present.

when.display: 8th century CE (Krishna I, c. 757-83); standing today

where.modern_name: Kailasa Temple, Ellora, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district, Maharashtra, India
where.historical_name: Great Kailasa at Elapura (Ellora), under the Rashtrakuta dynasty

importance.justification: The ASI calls it the largest single monolithic excavation in the world.

reviewer_note: Covers the Kailasa temple only; Ellora as a whole is place-ellora-caves. No model: the 32 m height (WHE) has no matching plan dimension on an opened page (the 90 m and 53 m figures describe the trenches, and the ASI gives no measurements). Shape would be stepped_pyramid or block. Least sure: start year (ASI and WHE give different reigns for Krishna I).
